removals.title: withdraw dust-handler silent override
removals.matchedTo: Known Issue #3: 'Dust prevention on withdrawal - withdrawing to below MINIMUM_STAKE forces full withdrawal'
removals.rationale: Exact behavioral match. The dust handler forcing a full withdrawal is the documented design. UX-event-emission suggestion alone (DEDUP-018's only remediation beyond revert) is not a security finding; the underlying behavior is acknowledged.

flagged.possibleMatch: KI-4 'pauseWithdraw does NOT claim rewards or update pool (emergency exit mechanism by design)'
flagged.note: Bare reward forfeiture aspect IS the known-issue acknowledgment. Kept because finding also covers (a) orphan per-share-accumulator residue with no defined redistribution semantics, (b) downstream un-rebased-debt that triggers DEDUP-002/DEDUP-003 reverts, neither of which is acknowledged. Report-writer may want to narrow framing to the orphan-redistribution + downstream-DoS angles.

flagged.possibleMatch: KI-7 'PhlimboEA requires minting rights on phUSD token (configuration requirement, not bug)'
flagged.note: KI-7 acknowledges the configuration requirement. Finding identifies no-try/catch and no-fallback design defect: sibling-side phUSD pause / revocation / supply-cap GLOBALLY bricks claim/stake/withdraw for any user with pending phUSD. Different framing — defect vs requirement. Kept; severity-classifier should decide whether to keep at Medium or fold into a 'cross-contract trust dependency' QA item.

flagged.possibleMatch: KI-6 'Pauser trust assumptions - designated pauser can pause/unpause contract operations'
flagged.note: On a strict reading, the root cause IS the acknowledged Pauser trust assumption — the finding sharpens it into a concrete selective-yield-denial pattern. Dedup notes flagged this as 'likely demoted to QA / centralization-report'. Kept and flagged; severity-classifier likely routes to centralization bundle, not standalone Medium.

Owner-touching findings (DEDUP-004, DEDUP-006, DEDUP-007) carve out structural defects rather than blanket centralization concerns.
